JOSE B. CATINDIG Sangguniang Panlungsod Member City of Santa Rosa, Laguna Dear Hon. Catindig: This pertains to your e-mail dated 14 September 2022 concerning the following legislative proposals: 1. AN ORDINANCE AMENDING AND STRENGTHENING THE SANTA ROSA COOPERATIVE DEVELOPMENT OFFICE (CDO) TO SANTA ROSA COOPERATIVE, LIVELIHOOD AND MICRO ENTERPRISE DEVELOPMENT OFFICE (CLMEDO) FOR THE CITY OF SANTA ROSA, LAGUNA. 2. AN ORDINANCE CREATING THE CITY ENTERPRISE MANAGEMENT AND DEVELOPMENT OFFICE (CEMDO) FOR THE PURPOSE OF ESTABLISHING, DEVELOPING, OPERATING, MAINTAINING AND MANAGING SUSTAINABLE CITY OWNED ENTERPRISES TO ENHANCE THE INCOME OF THE CITY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFORE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES. Relative thereto, the antecedent facts are as follows: • The proposed ordinances were said to have been crafted to better the bureaucracy and collection service of the various city economic enterprises and to amend and enhance the local government's cooperative office to adapt in a rapid changing economic environment and livelihood development. The Municipal Cooperative Development Office (MCDO), which is the subject matter of the first (ISt) proposed ordinance, was created in a form of a resolution in 2002. For the second (2nd) proposed ordinance, it was discovered that the previous Sanggunian passed an appropriation ordinance sometime in 2018-2022 on the insertion of "City Enterprise Management Development Office. However, it was alleged that the same was created without an enabling law and there was no clear mandate, function and staff compliment created. Hence, the proposed ordinance. However, during the committee hearing, some Sangguniang Panlungsod members and other invited panelists mentioned that the proposals are somewhat ultra vires and that the authority to create an office in the LGU is the sole power of the Mayor by virtue of the City charter of Santa Rosa. The suggestion of the other sanggunian members is to just pass a resolution requesting the city mayor to create an office or amend the resolution creating that office. The prevailing issue herein is on whether or not it is within the power of the local "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Tntnkline Nn • RR7R.q,-1.fitl

legislative body to pass an ordinance creating an office under the executive branch of the local government. We opine in the affirmative. The letter cited the salient provision of the City Charter of Santa Rosa that provides for the power of the sangguniang panlungsod to determine the powers and duties of the Officials and employees of the city. Section IO (g), Article IV, thereof, as cited in the City Councilor's letter, states: "Section IO — The Sangguniang Panlungsod g. Subject to the provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 and other pertinent laws, determine the powers and duties of the officials and employees of the City;" (Emphasis Supplied) The same is consistent with RA. No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, as Section 454 (c) thereof provides as follows: "(c) The Sanggunian Panlungsod may: (l) Maintain existing offices not mentioned in subsections (a) and (b) hereof; (2) Create such other offices may be necessary to carry out the purposes of the city government; or (3) Consolidate the functions of any office with those of another in the interest of efficiency and economy." (Emphasis Supplied) It is clear that both the City Charter of Santa Rosa, Laguna, and the Local Government Code provide for the authority of the Sanggunian Panlungsod to create offices that may be necessary to carry out the purposes of the city government. This creation is understood to be through an ordinance as the creation of a new office has a corresponding funding requirement that should be addressed by an appropriation therefor. It follows that the creation of office may include the mandate and function of the office sought to be created and the personnel complement needed in that office. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you.
